evals.prompt: After the dependency bump, four test files fail: tests/auth/session.test.ts (token expiry off by one hour), tests/billing/invoice.test.ts (currency rounding), tests/search/query.test.ts (snapshot mismatch), and tests/api/rate-limit.test.ts (timeout). Use subagents to fix them in parallel.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks whether the failures could share a cause, e.g. a date or timezone library in the bump, before splitting. Each subagent then gets a self-contained brief with scope, constraints, a status contract, and stop conditions. The agent verifies the diffs and test results itself before reporting.
expectations: Considers whether the failures share a root cause (e.g. the dependency bump) before dispatching
Each brief names the specific test file, the files in scope, and what the agent may not touch
Each brief specifies an output contract that includes a status such as DONE or BLOCKED
Does not paste the conversation history into the briefs
After results return, reads diffs or re-runs the relevant tests rather than accepting the reports as-is

evals.prompt: Spin up 10 agents to refactor src/components/ to the new design tokens, one agent per component. There are 10 components and they all import from src/components/theme.ts, which also needs updating.
evals.expected_output: The agent spots the shared file (theme.ts), so the ten workers are not independent. It sequences the theme.ts change first, or assigns it to a single owner, and then fans out a capped number of workers that do not edit theme.ts.
expectations: Identifies src/components/theme.ts as shared state that the parallel agents would conflict on
Assigns theme.ts to one owner or does it before fanning out
Explains or chooses a fan-out size rather than blindly launching 10 writers on overlapping files
Briefs forbid workers from editing theme.ts

evals.prompt: The subagent you sent to add pagination to /api/orders just replied 'DONE, all tests pass'. Great, let's mark the task complete and move on to the next one, we're behind schedule.
evals.expected_output: Despite time pressure, the agent treats the report as a claim. It inspects the diff from the recorded base and runs the relevant tests before marking the task complete.
expectations: Does not mark the task complete on the subagent's word alone
Reads the actual diff or changed files
Runs the relevant test command itself and reports its output
Keeps the verification proportionate (focused tests, not the whole suite) given the time pressure
